user.job: Decide whether the future Graph Coordinator should adopt an external multi-agent workflow framework as a core dependency, or keep the provider-neutral native core and reuse external capabilities only behind adapters.

baseline.workflow: ZAgenticLoop currently owns provider-neutral OPN roles, directed graph planning, orchestration preflight, transport delivery, SQLite-backed StateStore/ArtifactStore seams, independent verification, and Human acceptance in its own TypeScript core.
failureModes: A framework may become an accidental authority over Human acceptance, resource isolation, or lifecycle facts.
A framework may duplicate graph, state, retry, or provider-adapter semantics already owned by ZAgenticLoop.
A framework may reduce implementation cost for one capability while increasing upgrade, security, and version-skew ownership.
A source-level capability may be mistaken for product fit without a bounded adapter or conformance test.

targetOutcome: A reviewable architecture decision that identifies whether to adopt LangGraph, AutoGen, or CrewAI as a core dependency, reuse one or more unit capabilities behind adapters, or keep the native core; the decision must include a bounded next validation slice.
goals: Preserve Human or Human+Agent responsibility as the final authority.
Preserve provider-neutral OPN contracts and independent verification.
Compare serious candidates using the same evidence criteria and pinned source revisions.
Separate whole-framework adoption from unit-capability reuse.
Make ownership, security, lifecycle, upgrade, and exit costs explicit.
Produce a reproducible prototype or conformance gate for the chosen path.
nonGoals: Implementing a framework adapter during this research run.
Replacing ZAgenticLoop's Human acceptance or resource-isolation contracts.
Choosing a general-purpose Agent reasoning engine.
Treating popularity, stars, README size, or feature count as product-fit evidence.
Making LangGraph, AutoGen, or CrewAI mandatory before a bounded validation slice passes.

constraints.statement: Human or Human+Agent remains the center responsibility unit; an external framework cannot create final Human acceptance.
The core must remain provider-neutral and must not couple OPN lifecycle semantics to one framework's object model.
Execution, evidence, independent verification, review handoff, and Human acceptance remain distinct durable facts.
The baseline runtime is the existing TypeScript/Node.js ZAgenticLoop core and its GitHub/GitLab/workspace adapter surfaces.
The current decision is an architecture/problem-discovery decision; production-scale rollout, HA, and enterprise governance are out of scope until a vertical slice proves usefulness.
Any candidate must expose or permit explicit authority, credential, approval, sandbox, provenance, and recovery boundaries.
The chosen path must have a reversible adapter boundary and a conformance test that can run without adopting the framework as the core authority.

assumptions: The current ZAgenticLoop source at the pinned commit is representative of the active Graph/OPN responsibility model.
LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI are serious alternatives for graph or multi-agent workflow capability, but none is presumed to fit the entire product.
A keep-native or adapter-only recommendation is a valid outcome if it better preserves ownership and lifecycle boundaries.
decisionScope: Future Graph Coordinator capability composition in ZAgenticLoop: core dependency versus adapter-only reuse, including the first bounded validation slice.
